regional_assessment: Mediterranean to temperate Alpine gradient implies dual stress regimes: summer drought/heat in the south and potential chilling/frost in the north. Calibration data shows strong negative yield residuals for tmin < -2.29°C and tmax > 29.27°C, suggesting sensitivity to early season frost and late season heat stress. Precipitation is low (median 0.31 mm/day), indicating water availability is a critical limiting factor across the gradient.

candidates.agronomic_rationale: Targets the most statistically significant negative residual zone for minimum temperature (tmin < -2.29°C) while capturing the upper heat stress threshold (tmax > 29.27°C) and low precipitation events (< 1.0 mm/day) common in the dry southern Mediterranean zones.

Refines the minimum temperature threshold to -0.27°C (capturing broader chill risk) and aligns tmax threshold with the 90th percentile (31.27°C) to capture extreme heat events, maintaining the strict precipitation cutoff at 0.31 mm/day (median) to identify drought stress.

Adopts a conservative approach for frost by using 0.00°C as the tmin threshold to cover all freezing events, sets tmax at 30.00°C to capture the 75th percentile heat stress, and uses 2.67 mm/day (75th percentile) to identify moderate-to-high precipitation days where yield residuals remain negative.
